title: RH3 policy shared laxity: Reserved octets 6-7 and non-canonical Hdr Ext Len unchecked in C, Python, and Rust alike
description: P3, found by worker5 subagent correctness pass of project-LICHEN-worker6-hahk. RFC 6554 s3 reserves RH3 octets 6-7 (16 bits after CmprI/CmprE/Pad) but all three implementations check only octets 4-5: C schc_helpers.c:432 (packet[offset+4]==0 && packet[offset+5]==0), Python headers.py:128 (data[2],data[3] where data = packet[offset+2:]), Rust codec.rs:301-310. A packet with nonzero Reserved octets 6-7 is accepted everywhere; functionally harmless (addresses start at octet 8; upper_destination read end-16 unaffected). Related laxity: address count uses floor division ((ext_len-8)/16 in C :436, (len(data)-6)//16 in Python :131, same in Rust :311), so a non-canonical Hdr Ext Len (e.g. HEL=3, 1 address + 8 trailing octets) is accepted with upper_destination landing on address-low-half + trailing garbage; RFC 6554 requires HEL == 2n when CmprI=CmprE=Pad=0, so HEL=3 is not expressible. Sender/receiver stay checksum-consistent (both use last-16), so this is RFC-conformance laxity, not a parity divergence. Fix needs COORDINATED changes in all three implementations plus new vectors (reserved-octets-nonzero, hel-non-canonical); C matches the references exactly today so no cross-impl break - decide whether njdx's canonical policy intended full Reserved-zero and tighten everywhere or document the shared laxity.
